I am 63 years old and I have farmed the land in Quzhou County since I was a young girl. I never went to school, but I know this soil and I know what works. My family has about 6 mu of land in total. Every year I follow the rotation that our village has used for generations.

My main field is 5 mu, and on that land I grow winter wheat and then summer maize. The wheat is already in the ground from last October. When the weather warms up I will spread ammonium bicarbonate and compound fertilizer on it as topdressing, and I will irrigate it three more times from the well before we harvest in early June. I save some of my own wheat seed, but I also buy improved seed from the shop when my own is not enough. Before sowing wheat in autumn I always use the rotary tiller to prepare the field.

After we cut the wheat in June, I will immediately sow hybrid maize seed on that same 5 mu. I do not till the soil for the maize anymore — I learned years ago that no-tillage saves me a lot of labor and fuel, and the maize still grows well if I manage the weeds. I use compound fertilizer for the maize and irrigate it twice during the summer. I expect the maize to yield better than the wheat.

I also keep 1 mu separate for cotton. Cotton is more work because the insects come constantly, but the price is decent and I have grown it for many years so I know the rhythm of it. I will rotary till that plot in spring, plant the cotton, and apply fertilizer. I will need to spray for pests many times on the cotton — more than the wheat or maize — but that is just the nature of cotton.

I do everything based on what I have seen work year after year. I do not try new fancy methods because at my age I cannot afford to take risks with my family's food and income.
